claim: Let \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\) be a finite connected complete multipartite graph with \(r\ge2\), \(N=\sum_i n_i\), \(L=\max_i n_i\), and let \(k\ge1\). A \(k\)-tuple total dominator coloring exists exactly when \(k\le N-L\). For feasible \(k\), define \[\tau=\min\left\{t\ge1:r\le k+t\le\sum_{i=1}^r\min\{n_i,t\}\right\}.\] Then \(\chi_{k,d}^t(G)=k+\tau\). Every optimal coloring is obtained by choosing integers \(c_i\) with \(1\le c_i\le\min\{n_i,\tau\}\) and \(\sum_i c_i=k+\tau\), and partitioning part \(i\) into exactly \(c_i\) nonempty color classes. With labeled colors, the number of optimal colorings is \[(k+\tau)!\sum_{\substack{1\le c_i\le\min\{n_i,\tau\}\\\sum_i c_i=k+\tau}}\prod_{i=1}^r \left\{\!\!\begin{matrix}n_i\\c_i\end{matrix}\!\!\right\},\] where the braces denote Stirling numbers of the second kind. In particular, if \(1\le k\le r-1\) then \(\chi_{k,d}^t(G)=r\), while for \(K_{m,n}\) with \(m\le n\) and \(1\le k\le m\), one has \(\chi_{k,d}^t(K_{m,n})=2k\).
integrity: The proof is self-contained. Exhaustive computation checks finite instances and the exact counting formula but is not used to justify the infinite quantifiers.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to complete multipartite graphs and minimum-color k-tuple total dominator colorings.
No value is assigned when k exceeds the minimum degree N-L, because no k-tuple total dominator coloring exists.
The k=1 specialization belongs to the established total dominator coloring theory and is not claimed as new.
The full text of the 2025 initiating article was unavailable in the public sources inspected; possible hidden overlap there remains a residual originality risk.
title: Exact k-tuple total dominator colorings of complete multipartite graphs
